To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel bidirectional multilvel boost-buck converter has been presented and analyzed.

a novel bidirectional multistage boost-buck dc converter topology is presented that is applicable when both sides need the same grounding, it has the advantage of bidirectional power flow, and it has a simplified topology for unidirectional applications.
a new bidirectional noninverting boostbuck dc-dc topology is presented and a new pulse width modulation strategy is proposed for dc-link capacitor voltage balancing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, implementation and evaluation of the proposed converter, which is an attractive option to be used in a wide variety of dc-dc power conversion applications, such as in renewable energy sources systems and electric vehicles.

the development of new multilevel converters for bidirectional power flow applications with reduced semiconductor devices losses, improved power quality, and reduced size and weight of passive components.
the analysis, design, and control of a novel bidirectional multilvel boost-buck converter, which is suitable for high power applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed converter has a very good performance in terms of efficiency, voltage and current stress, and is a very promising alternative to the conventional boost-buck converter in applications where bidirectional power flow is required.
the multilevel boost converter has the potential to be a good alternative for the boost converter, especially in high voltage applications.
multilevel converters are the future in power electronics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the novel converter is suitable for applications where bidirectional power flow, low voltage ripple, high voltage gain, low semiconductor losses and small dc-link capacitance are required.
the proposed multilevel boost–buck converter is an interesting option to be used in bidirectional applications where the dc-link voltage is required to be the same on both sides of the converters.
the multilevel topology is an attractive solution for bidirectional dc-dc applications with the same grounding at the input and output.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multilevel boost converters are a good option for applications requiring a bidirectional power flow and/or a low voltage ripple at the dc link.

the proposed multilevel converter topology can be used in applications where bidirectional power flow is required and the dc link voltage is limited by the available voltage rating of the semiconductor devices, such as the electric vehicle power train.
the proposed converter is an interesting solution for bidirectional power flow and voltage balancing applications.
